paper_metadata.title: Optimized mechanical properties of titanium-oxygen alloys by powder metallurgy
paper_metadata.journal: journal of materials research and technology

evidence.quote: Oxygen solid solution-strengthened titanium-oxygen (Ti eO) alloys with ultrahigh yield strength and large ductility were designed and synthesized via high-energy ball milling (BM) combined with spark plasma sintering (SPS) in compression.
The effects of the sintering temperature and added oxygen content resulted in Ti eO alloys with ultra-high strength and large ductility.

BM was performed continuously for 1 h using a high-energy BM machine (SPEX 8000 M) in an Ar atmosphere with a liquid process control agent (C 18H36O2). The rotating speed was set up to 1725 r/min, and the ball-to-powder mass ratio was 1:1.

The compacted powder was then sintered using SPS (SPS-20T-10-IV, Shanghai Chenhua Science and Technology Corp., Ltd., China) at sintering temperatures of 950, 1000, or 1050 /C14 C for 1 h under an axial pressure of 30 MPa.

It is generally assumed that oxygen is only found as a solid solution in titanium alloys [26e29] and that titanium ( a phase) with a hexagonal close-packed (hcp) structure can incorporate up to 15 wt% oxygen [30].
The precipitation of more b-phases in the Ti eO alloy sintered at 1000 /C14 C compared to the alloy sintered at 950 /C14 C hindered grain growth and coarsening.
The grain size of the alloys with different oxygen contents is approximately 30 mm and the matrix consisted of equiaxed crystals.
The Ti-1.5 at% O alloy (UBM) sintered at 1000 /C14 C exhibits a porous morphology.

Only a few pores are observed in the Ti-1.5 at% O alloy (BM). These samples exhibited a smaller porosity than that of the UBM alloy because of the tight arrangement of particles during the SPS process.
Dimples are observed only in the BM alloys, indicating that the samples absorbed some energy from the shear bands during the fracture process.
